newsitem.title: USA: U.S. public supports legal services for poor.
newsitem.headline: U.S. public supports legal services for poor.

text.p: A majority of Americans believe federal funds should be used to pay for civil legal services to the poor in cases such as child custody, adoption and divorce, according to a survey released Thursday.

The results of the Louis Harris & Associates poll, released during the American Bar Association annual meeting, showed that 70 percent of Americans believe federal funding should be provided to low income people who need help in civil cases. The poll was conducted last month.

Survey participants were also asked if they would support spending $1.50 of taxpayer dollars per person annually to fund the Legal Services Corporation, which provides civil legal service to the poor.
Sixty-one percent said they would support such spending.

The House Appropriations Committee, which has jurisdiction over Legal Services Corporation funding, voted earlier this month to cut LSC funding by 50 percent. This reduction is on top of a 33 percent cut last year in funds for the agency.
"Congress should listen to the American public and preserve the Legal Services Corporation," said ABA President N. Lee Cooper.
"Without this access only the rich own the key to the courthouse door in America. Justice should not be for sale to the highest bidder," Cooper said.
